issue.title: Null pointer dereference in `_sqlite` cursor cache via re-entrant parameter iterator

labels.name: extension-modules
labels.description: C modules in the Modules dir

labels.name: type-crash
labels.description: A hard crash of the interpreter, possibly with a core dump

comments.body:
Many such reports use the word "re-entrant". I do not think it means what you think it means. A re-entrant call is
when a function, while still executing its first call, is called again (either recursively or by another thread/process).

Hi @serhiy-storchaka, thank you for bringing this up!

I understand "reentrant" has a precise technical definition that the same function being entered twice before the first invocation completes. However, I'm using it in a broader sense here to describe a related pattern: the interpreter frame being entered twice (when an opcode handler that dispatched from a interpreter frame invokes user-overridden/overwritten/provided code that gets interpreted again).

I'm drawing from [CWE-1265: Unintended Reentrant Invocation of Non-reentrant Code Via Nested Calls](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1265.html), which describes a similar issue pattern. That said, I recognize there may be a more precise term for this specific bug pattern in the Python interpreter context.

Would you suggest an alternative term that better captures this nested interpreter invocation pattern? I'm open to adjusting the terminology if "reentrant" feels too broad or potentially misleading here.
